kurz: Where the leverage of a futures contract comes from, why gains and losses are settled daily and what rolling costs.

bloecke.md:
An option gives its buyer a right. A futures contract, by contrast, creates an obligation for both sides. The buyer of a DAX future undertakes to take delivery of the index at the agreed futures price, and the seller undertakes to deliver it. With the DAX, nothing is physically delivered; settlement is in cash. Because neither side acquires a right, nobody pays a premium either. A futures contract has a value of zero when it is entered into, because the futures price is set so that buying and selling are worth the same at that moment.

There is therefore no purchase price and thus no natural amount that you have put in. Most misunderstandings about futures stem from this. The risk is measured by the notional value of the contract and not by the amount tied up in the account. For Eurex index futures, this notional value is large.

bloecke.titel: Point value and notional value of Eurex index futures

bloecke.md: The notional values are calculated for a DAX level of 26,000 points. The index reached its all-time high to date at the end of August 2026, at just over 26,500 points. The FDAX runs in a quarterly cycle of March, June, September and December, with maturities of up to 36 months. It expires on the third Friday of the expiry month at 13:00 CET, and the final settlement price comes from the Xetra auction at the same time. The EURO STOXX 50 future closes at 12:00 CET and is settled at the average of the index calculations between 11:50 and 12:00. Eurex transaction fees are €1.50 per FDAX contract in the standard case. Trading itself is therefore cheap; the problems with futures lie elsewhere.

The margin deposit shows how much collateral the clearing house requires. It does not show how much is at risk, because the risk is measured by the notional value. A position size that is based only on the margin therefore rests on no risk calculation at all.

## Three types of margin

The **initial margin** is the collateral that must be deposited when a position is opened. The **maintenance margin** is the minimum balance the account must hold for the position to remain open. It is below the initial margin so that not every small price movement immediately triggers a margin call. The **variation margin** is a payment and not collateral. At the end of every trading day, the position is valued at the settlement price, and the day's gain or loss is credited to or debited from the account. For the FDAX, this settlement price is the volume-weighted average of all trades in the minute before 17:30 CET.

Eurex Clearing calculates the collateral on a portfolio basis using the Prisma model and adjusts it daily to the risk. There is therefore no fixed euro amount per contract, and brokers regularly add a buffer of their own to the clearing house's requirement. The following calculation works with assumed but plausibly sized values: one Mini-DAX future, initial margin €9,000, maintenance margin €8,000, account balance €12,000. The initial margin thus corresponds to just under 7% of the notional value, and relative to the capital employed, the effective leverage is around eleven.

bloecke.titel: Long position in a Mini-DAX future over ten trading days (illustrative calculation)
Account balance and margin thresholds over ten trading days
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with assumed margin rates. On days 5 and 6 the account balance fell below the maintenance margin; for the following days it is assumed that the account was topped up to €9,000 each time.

bloecke.md:
At the end, the index is back at its starting level, so the position has earned nothing. Nevertheless, €2,600 had to be paid in along the way. Without these payments, the position would have been forcibly closed out on the fifth or sixth day, that is, at the most unfavourable moment shortly before the recovery. The fall from 26,000 to 24,880 points is an index loss of 4.3%. In the account, that is 1,120 points times €5, which comes to €5,600 or 47% of the capital. This calculation shows the effect of leverage.

With a full FDAX, the same movement would have amounted to €28,000. A book loss in an equity portfolio can be just as large as a loss on a future. The difference lies in when it falls due. The book loss is only realised when the shares are sold; the loss on the future is debited from the account the same evening.

bloecke.titel: No negative balance protection for futures
bloecke.md: The negative balance protection prescribed by ESMA and the obligation to close out at 50% of the minimum margin apply to CFDs and not to exchange-traded futures. If the loss from an overnight price gap exceeds the collateral deposited, a debt to the broker arises that the investor must settle. More important than the amount of margin required is therefore the question of how large a loss an overnight event can trigger. A stop does not protect against such a price jump either.

## Convergence, contango and the costs of rolling

On the expiry date, the futures price must equal the spot price, because the settlement price is derived from the spot market. Before that, it may deviate from the spot price, namely by the costs of holding the underlying until maturity.

bloecke.formel: F − S = Interest + Storage costs − Convenience yield
bloecke.erklaerung: The difference between the futures price and the spot price results from a cost calculation and is not a forecast. If F is above S, this is called contango; if F is below it, backwardation.
variablen: storage, insurance, shrinkage (only for physical commodities)
benefit of physical possession, such as security of supply
bloecke.beispiel: DAX total return index at 26,000 points, remaining term three months, financing at the ECB deposit facility rate of 2.50%: F ≈ 26,000 × (1 + 0.025 × 0.25) = 26,163 points, that is, around 163 points above the spot price.

bloecke.titel: Contango and backwardation with the same spot price
bloecke.unter: Schematic, not market data. Both curves start at the spot price of $70. The contango curve contains a mark-up for storage and interest; in the backwardation curve, a premium is paid for immediate availability.

bloecke.md: A futures contract has a fixed expiry date. To hold a position permanently, you have to close the expiring contract before each expiry and open the next one (rolling). In contango, the old contract is sold more cheaply at every roll than the new one is bought. This is due to the shape of the futures curve and not to bad luck or poor execution.

bloecke.titel: Roll loss with a constant spot price
bloecke.md:
The spot price stays constant at $70.00 for a year. The front-month future is quoted at $70.80 throughout. It is bought at 70.80, and by maturity the contract converges to 70.00. The loss per roll is 0.80 / 70.80 = 1.13%.

With twelve rolls, the result is 0.9887 to the power of 12 = 0.873. So 100 becomes 87.3. That is a loss of 12.7%, even though the underlying has not moved by a single cent. Fees, the spread and the management fee of an ETP come on top.

bloecke.titel: Rolled long position with an unchanged spot price, index = 100
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with permanent contango of 1.13% per roll and twelve rolls. The same roll loss weighs on commodity and volatility ETPs held over the long term.

bloecke.md: A textbook example is the USO oil fund. In 2009 the spot price of crude oil rose strongly, while the fund, because of constant rolling in a steep contango curve, captured only a fraction of this rise. Products on VIX futures are subject to the same effect; their futures curve is almost always in contango in calm phases. For holding periods of more than a few weeks, the result of such ETPs therefore depends more on the shape of the futures curve than on the performance of the underlying.

The DAX is a total return index in which dividends are already notionally reinvested. No dividend is therefore deducted in the futures price, and the gap to the spot price results essentially from the financing rate. With positive interest rates, the futures curve is therefore usually in contango. In the period of negative interest rates in the euro area, from 2014 to 2022, the futures price was by contrast mostly below the spot price (backwardation).

The EURO STOXX 50, on which the FESX is based, is a price return index without dividends. Here, F ≈ S × (1 + r·T) − expected dividends until maturity. European companies pay out their dividends mainly in the spring. FESX contracts whose term extends beyond this dividend season are therefore regularly quoted below the index. This discount results arithmetically from the expected dividends and is not a forecast of falling prices.

punkte: Hedging existing holdings whose size matches the contract value
Quickly adjusting the equity allocation without restructuring an entire portfolio
Index exposure without buying securities, while the capital earns interest elsewhere
A company's commodity and interest rate risks that cannot be traded any other way
A substitute for capital, to bring a portfolio that is too small up to index size with leverage
A directional bet with a stop that an overnight price gap jumps over
Buy-and-hold on commodities or volatility via rolled contracts
Sizing positions by margin instead of by maximum loss

bloecke.md:
## Suitability for private investors

Even the smallest contract in the DAX family controls a notional value of €26,000 at 26,000 points. For hedging a portfolio of €30,000 that is a coarse fit, and for speculating with an account of €5,000 it is disproportionate. In addition, daily settlement requires a liquidity buffer that must not be invested. Access requires the account to be enabled for derivative transactions (Termingeschäfte), and before that the broker must assess appropriateness under Section 63(10) WpHG (Securities Trading Act). A roll is also due every three months. It costs spread and fees and brings the risk of trading in the illiquid phase shortly before expiry.

For pure index investment, an ETF is suitable; for hedging a portfolio, the put from the previous lesson. The simplest way to achieve less risk is a lower equity allocation. Futures are intended for positions that already have the size of a contract. They are not suitable for accounts that only reach this size through the future.

Gains and losses from futures fall under Section 20(2) sentence 1 no. 3 EStG (Income Tax Act) as derivative transactions. They are taxed at 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) plus solidarity surcharge, that is, at 26.375% without church tax (Section 32d(1) EStG). The former limit on loss offsetting of €20,000 a year (Section 20(6) sentence 5 EStG, old version) was abolished without replacement by the Annual Tax Act 2024 (Jahressteuergesetz) and no longer applies in any open cases (Section 52(28) EStG). Losses go into the general loss pot (allgemeiner Verlusttopf) and not into the share loss pot, which only applies to sales of shares (Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG). They are carried forward indefinitely but may never be offset against wages or rental income. With foreign brokers, nobody withholds tax, and the income then belongs in the capital income annex (Anlage KAP). This overview is no substitute for tax advice.

mitnehmen: The leverage of a futures contract results from the contract size, €25 per index point for the FDAX, and does not depend on how little margin is deposited.
The variation margin is a payment and not a valuation, so losses are debited the same evening and the position can be liquidated before the expected price movement occurs.
If the index returns to its starting point, the future yields no profit, but it may require several top-up payments along the way.
In contango, every roll causes a loss, even with an unchanged spot price, and over twelve months 1.13% per roll adds up to a loss of around 13%.
There is no negative balance protection for exchange-traded futures, so the loss can exceed the collateral deposited.

begriffe.text: Collateral that must be deposited when a futures position is opened. It is a pledge and not a purchase price. The clearing house sets its amount on a risk basis.
Daily settlement of the gain and loss of a futures position at the settlement price. Unlike a book loss, the amount is debited from or credited to the account as a payment.
Minimum balance that a margin account must have. If the balance falls below it, a margin call follows. If the top-up payment is not made, the position is forcibly closed out.
Market situation with a futures price above the spot price, usual where there are financing and storage costs. For a rolled long position, this results in a structural roll loss.
Market situation with a futures price below the spot price, typical in times of scarcity or a high convenience yield. A rolled long position then earns a positive roll yield.
